figures.caption: Figure 3: Prequential accuracy on BCIC 2a for ACM+TS+SVM, frozen vs. online refit (9 subjects; bold curves are the across-subject mean, shaded bands the standard error, thin curves individual subjects). Left: trailingwindow accuracy Ak (Eq. 2, w = 25). Right: cumulative accuracy Ck (Eq. 1). Online refit remains above frozen for most of the stream and the advantage grows over time.
Figure 4: Training-sample contribution analysis on BCIC. Left: paired tests comparing summed Shapley values across training blocks. Right: influence profile as a function of temporal distance.

Figure 5: Exact block-level (part) Shapley value on BCIC 2a. The 432-trial training pool is split into P = 6 contiguous temporal blocks (oldest to newest), each treated as a single Shapley player, so the value is computed by exact enumeration of all 26 coalitions. Bars are the across-run mean ± standard error for FBCSP and ACM+TS+SVM. The newest blocks receive the largest credit in both pipelines.

Figure 6: Cross-dataset comparison of the exact block-level Shapley valuation. The newest temporal block carries the largest mean value in both pipelines and on both datasets; the gradient is flatter on the small ALEXMI stream and sharper on the larger Schirrmeister 2017 streams.

Figure 7: Smoothed signed helpful influence versus train–test temporal distance for a single subject (subject 1, seed 0). Values above zero are helpful, below zero harmful. FBCSP is slightly positive at short distances and turns negative in the far tail, whereas ACM+TS+SVM stays much closer to zero across the axis, indicating that FBCSP is more sensitive to temporal distance for this subject.
